post.caption:
Hallucination is not lying, it is the mechanism working as designed. The model predicts likely continuations rather than retrieving verified facts, and an invented answer that reads exactly right is a very good prediction. That is why fabricated citations are so convincing: a real one has an author, year, journal and plausible title, and so does a fake one, with nothing in the process checking that the paper exists. Retrieval and tool use help. So does being most suspicious when it sounds most authoritative.
